reference: GNU coreutils comm is run on the same small, sorted relative fixture files inside the mandatory isolated runner. The metadata contract uses Bash's documented type -t builtin result.
coverage: Three-column merge with duplicate records and records unique to each input.
Combined column suppression, including the no-prefix rule when earlier columns are suppressed.
Custom output delimiters and the GNU --total summary counts.
NUL-delimited records, unterminated final records, and stdin as the first input.
Explicit sorted-order failure and --nocheck-order behavior on unsorted fixture data.
Missing operand and missing relative input-file errors.
Bash metadata: comm is available as a builtin with an empty candidate PATH.
exclusions: Write-failure behavior against device-backed sinks is omitted; all fixture paths remain relative and regular-file based.
Exact diagnostic wording is not asserted where GNU and Bash loadable prefixes may differ; error presence, status, output, and fixture tree are compared.
